# Implementation Plan: PDF Link Reader and Prompt-to-Word Agent

**Branch**: `001-pdf-to-word-agent` | **Date**: 2026-03-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-pdf-to-word-agent/spec.md`

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit.plan`. Execution workflow reference: `.specify/templates/plan-template.md`.

## Summary

Deliver a **Spring Boot** service that (1) downloads a PDF from a user-supplied HTTPS URL, validates PDF type, and returns **extracted text**; (2) accepts a **natural-language prompt** and optional PDF text context, calls an **LLM** via **Spring AI**, and returns a **`.docx`** file to the client so users can save it to a **local folder** (browser or `curl`). The public HTTP contract is documented in **OpenAPI 3.2.0** (`contracts/openapi.yaml`). Operations ship as a **Docker** image suitable for **EKS/ECS**. See `research.md` for technology decisions and `quickstart.md` for run instructions.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Java 25 (LTS)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Spring Boot 4.0.x, Spring Web/WebFlux (**WebClient** for PDF fetch), JDK **HttpClient** for OpenAI Chat Completions (Spring AI deferred until Boot 4 BOM alignment), Apache PDFBox, Apache POI (XWPF), Springdoc OpenAPI 3; **when durable storage is required**, use **Spring Data JPA** (or JDBC) with **PostgreSQL** and **Flyway** or **Liquibase**  
**Storage**: MVP stays stateless (temp files only). **If a database is introduced** (job history, audit, async tasks, multi-step sessions), use **PostgreSQL** as the only supported RDBMS unless an explicit future ADR says otherwise (see `research.md`, `data-model.md`)  
**Testing**: JUnit 5, Mockito, `@WebMvcTest`, MockWebServer or WebClient test support for PDF fetch  
**Target Platform**: Linux containers on **EKS** or **ECS**; local macOS/Linux dev  
**Project Type**: HTTP API (backend service)  
**Performance Goals**: PDF fetch + extract typical ≤ 60s within limits; generation p95 ≤ 5 minutes under normal provider latency (per success criteria)  
**Constraints**: Max PDF download size 25 MB (configurable); OpenAPI **3.2.0** for HTTP APIs; Maven-only build; Dockerfile-based deployment  
**Scale/Scope**: Single-tenant interactive use per deployment for v1; horizontal scale via stateless replicas (no session affinity required if no in-memory session added)
